Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, Git-Bash/PowerShell environment). Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies allowed (icon files are static assets, not packages).

CONTEXT — two independent research passes already confirmed the plan, don't re-derive it, just execute it:
- lib/assets/icons.ts currently has ~147 hand-authored icons across 9 categories. lib/assets/provenance.ts documents (module-level, not per-asset) that everything today is original work, and explicitly states the prerequisite for adding anything third-party: "a per-asset source/license/author/URL record, a license field the tool output can carry, a brand/trademark flag" must exist BEFORE any vendored asset is added. Read lib/assets/provenance.ts in full — it names its own requirements precisely; follow them.
- docs/research/asset-sources.md (§4 "Recommendation") and an independent audit both converged on the same answer: vendor raw SVG source from Lucide (ISC + partial MIT for Feather-derived icons), Tabler Icons (MIT), Phosphor Icons (MIT), and Heroicons (MIT) — all sourced from their own official GitHub repos (lucide-icons/lucide, tabler/tabler-icons, phosphor-icons/core, tailwindlabs/heroicons), never from aggregators (iconoop, svgrepo, GitHub mirror repos) which mix in unverifiable or non-permissive licenses (Font Awesome and coolicons are CC BY 4.0 — attribution required — and must be excluded; any brand/logo icon sets are a trademark issue independent of copyright and must also be excluded).
- The concrete problem being solved: lib/assets/icons.ts's `services`/`trades` category has only 22 icons, and its SYNONYMS map resolves five completely different trade businesses (plumber, plumbing, electrician, handyman, mechanic/garage) all down to the same single `wrench` icon. `contact` has only 10 icons total, shared by every generated site's contact section. This is a real, structural sameness problem, not just an aesthetic one.

YOUR JOB:

## Step 1 — build the provenance infrastructure first (the stated prerequisite)
Read lib/assets/provenance.ts's exact stated requirements and implement them: add a per-asset provenance record capability (source repo name, upstream icon id, license string, upstream version/commit or release tag, retrieved-at date) that the icon catalogue's existing `Entry`/render machinery can carry, and a brand/trademark exclusion mechanism (a boolean flag or category that keeps anything logo/brand-mark-like out of what the model can place autonomously — Lucide/Tabler/Phosphor/Heroicons are all general UI icon sets, not brand-logo packs, so this should mostly be a not-applicable/false flag for everything you vendor here, but the mechanism itself must exist for future use). Update provenance.ts's own module-level claims to accurately reflect that some assets are now vendored-with-recorded-provenance rather than 100% original work — do not leave the file asserting something no longer true.

## Step 2 — source the actual icon files
Fetch real SVG source directly from each project's official GitHub repository (use WebFetch/git — whichever tool actually gets you the raw files; these are real permissively-licensed open-source projects, this is legitimate vendoring, not scraping an unverified site). For each of the four packs:
1. Confirm the LICENSE file's content directly from the repo (don't trust a cached memory of what it says — fetch and read it now) and save a copy locally (e.g. lib/assets/icon-licenses/<pack>/LICENSE).
2. Record the exact commit/tag/version you pulled from.
3. Pull a curated, targeted set of icons that actually fill the gaps found — prioritize the `services`/`trades` and `contact` categories specifically (e.g., real distinct icons for plumbing/pipes, electrical/circuit, carpentry, painting, landscaping, HVAC, cleaning, security, IT/tech support, real distinct additional contact-method icons beyond the current 10) rather than importing entire packs wholesale — this is about closing specific convergence gaps, not maximizing total icon count. A few hundred well-chosen icons across the weak categories is the right scale, not thousands.
4. Exclude anything resembling a brand/company logo from any of the four packs (Tabler and Phosphor in particular sometimes include brand-adjacent icons — check and exclude).

## Step 3 — integrate into the catalogue
Add the vendored icons into lib/assets/icons.ts (or a clearly-named sibling module, following whatever pattern is more consistent with how the existing 147 are organized — read the file's actual structure before deciding) as real `IconDef`-shaped entries with real geometry (not re-drawn/approximated — use the actual upstream path data), each carrying the new provenance record from Step 1. Give them sensible keywords/synonyms so `findAssets()`'s existing token-scoring actually surfaces them for the gap terms identified above (e.g. a real "pipe wrench" or "electrical panel" icon should now outrank the generic wrench for an electrician-specific query, and the SYNONYMS map should be updated so `plumber`/`electrician`/`handyman`/`mechanic` resolve to genuinely different icons instead of all converging on one). Update lib/agent.ts's asset-catalogue description (the "~460 inlinable assets" line) to reflect the new real total once you know it.

## Constraints
- Every vendored icon must have a real, traceable provenance record. No icon without one.
- Exclude anything CC BY (Font Awesome, coolicons) or otherwise non-permissive, and anything brand/logo-shaped.
- Do not touch icons.ts's existing 147 original icons' geometry — pure addition, no modification of existing entries.
- Do not touch anything in the font/design-plan work already done (lib/fonts/, the design-plan section of lib/agent.ts) or the multi-page fix already done (lib/wizard.ts, lib/templates.ts) — if your changes to lib/agent.ts are near either of those, keep your edit narrowly scoped to just the asset-count line.
- Keep the total added payload reasonable — this is inlined SVG source that gets pasted into generated sites' code, not loaded over a network, so bloating the catalogue with thousands of rarely-used icons adds real token cost to every future generation for no benefit. Favor filling the identified gaps precisely over maximizing count.

## Verification
Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish. Also do a quick sanity check: call/trace through `findAssets("plumber")`, `findAssets("electrician")`, and `findAssets("mechanic")` (read the code path, or use a small script if one already exists for testing the catalogue) and confirm they no longer all resolve to the same single icon.

Report back: exactly how many icons you added from each pack, the exact license/version for each, how the provenance record is structured, and the before/after result of the plumber/electrician/mechanic search-convergence check.
